source_text: Quod cum ita sit atque huic tu loco miserrime obnitaris, incertum est, quid magis de te aestimari conveniat, utrum contra conscientiam tuam falsa defendas an, quod falsum est, esse verum putes ac per hoc sit incertum, utrum oculos rationis amiseris, dum certum sit oculos te fidei perdidisse.
pass_a_gloss: Which since it is so and you most miserably strive against this place, it is uncertain what more it is fitting to be estimated of you, whether you defend false things against your conscience or think that which is false to be true, and through this it is uncertain whether you have lost the eyes of reason, while it is certain that you have destroyed the eyes of faith.

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Since this is so, and you resist this point so miserably, it is uncertain which judgment better fits you: that you defend falsehood against your conscience, or think what is false to be true. Thus whether you have lost the eyes of reason remains uncertain, while it is certain that you have lost the eyes of faith.

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
